tutorial.text: This is your store now. Before we expand, let’s spruce up Grandma’s konbini: products, a manager and services.
Onigiri, Bentō and drinks are our bread and butter. Watch your margins, but don’t push prices too high or customers will head to our rivals.
Every store needs a manager to look after the team and daily business. Good people skills keep customers happy; marketing skills bring more shoppers in.
Shironeko Express parcel services, an ATM or ticket sales earn commission and bring in people who often grab a coffee too.
Book campaigns in the marketing tab, from neighbourhood flyers to city billboards. Start small and see what works.
These are your BuuHuu ratings. More ghosts mean more customers. Cleanliness, choice, wait times and prices all count.
The first customers are coming back to Grandma's Store! From now on, you’ll get weekly results and the latest Konbini Shimbun.
Oh dear, we lost money this week. That’s normal at first. Check your manager, prices and products — we’ll get there!
We have enough cash for a second store! Grandma’s little konbini is becoming a real chain.
Grandma's Store is up and running! Time for a second branch. See those “To let” pins on the map? Tap one to take a look. Hurry, though — our rivals won’t wait!
Here’s the weekly rent, deposit and foot traffic for your second store. More passers-by mean more customers, but higher rent too.
Let’s fit out the second store: facade, interior and equipment. A chilled display and coffee machine are required. An oden pot shines in winter. You’ll see the full cost at the end.
The builders are getting started! Your second store opens in a few weeks. Meanwhile, Grandma's Store keeps earning cash.
That’s all from me for now. I’m always here if you need me. Gambatte!

story.text: Irasshaimase! I’m Kobo. This little store in {startviertel} belonged to your grandma. For decades, she served onigiri, warm tea and a kind word for everyone.
Now it’s yours. Grandma also left you 5 million yen. It’s not much, but it’s enough for a good start.
Watch out: other young companies are opening their first stores in {stadt} too. Every free spot they take is one you can’t have.
There are currently 20 free stores in the city. A few more appear each year, but fewer over time. First come, first served!
Let’s turn Grandma's Store into the biggest konbini chain in {stadt}! I’m by your side. Gambatte!

hinweise.text: Oh no, your cash has been shrinking for 4 weeks! Check your products, prices and manager. A promotion might help too.
Careful, your balance is negative! Stay in the red for 4 weeks and it’s game over. Cut costs or lower prices to attract shoppers. {wochen} weeks left!
Your balance stayed negative for 4 weeks, so the chain has to close. Chin up: Grandma started small too. Give it another go!
Your prices are too high and customers are staying away. Lower them a little and people will come back!
Oden, Bentō and seasonal goods have good margins. Add them to your range!
Cash is tight. Cancel services and contracts that aren’t worth it. There’s a one-off ¥50,000 fee, but you’ll save every week. A bank loan can help if things stay tight.
Stop expensive campaigns until your balance is positive again.
Wait until you have a cash buffer before building again. One store too many can cost you the whole chain.
Phew, we made it! Cash is positive again. Grandma would be proud!
